case_title.value: Go Pal v. State of Karnataka

quotes.text: GO PAL v. STATE OF KARNATAKA
The appellant - Gopal challenges his conviction under Section 302 l.P.C. in this appeal.
The allegation against the appellant-accused are that on 29.12.1998 at about 5 p.m., he poured kerosene on the body of his wife Mallavva and set her on fire.

neutral_facts.value: The accused poured kerosene on the body of his wife and set her on fire. The victim was rushed to the hospital, where a doctor informed the police. The victim later succumbed to her injuries. The police recorded the victim's dying declaration, which alleged that the accused had a history of drinking and quarreling with her, and that on the day of the incident, he demanded money back, leading to an altercation where he poured kerosene on her and set her ablaze. The forensic science laboratory report confirmed the presence of kerosene residue on the victim's clothing, supporting the version in the dying declaration.

The victim was rushed to hospital. The doctor, PW-5 intimated the police station. The police officer, PW-13 recorded the statement of the victim. After few days, the victim succumbed to the burn injuries.
The trial court convicted the appellant under Section 302 ~PC. The High Court upheld the same.

key_evidence_accepted.value: The Supreme Court accepted the dying declaration as the sole basis for the conviction, supported by the presence of kerosene residue on the victim's garments and the FSL Report.

quotes.text: The dying declaration recorded by PW-13 and supported by PW-5 and the endorsement made by him to the effect that the victim was in a fit mental condition to depose before the police convinces that the dying declaration itself was a good dying declaration and could have been acted upon.

witness_credibility.value: The court noted that the witnesses who carried the deceased to the hospital turned hostile, but this did not undermine the credibility of the dying declaration as the circumstances strongly supported the version given in the declaration.

quotes.text: The witnesses, who carried the deceased to the hospital, turned hostile during their examinations but that may not be an escape route for the accused because the man may lie but the circumstances do not.

legal_principle_applied.value: The Supreme Court applied the principle that a dying declaration can be the sole basis for conviction if it is corroborated by other evidence and the circumstances support its authenticity.
